title: RAW UNREVIEWED: two source words share matched letter columns while paid left/right roles preserve both spellings
summary: Invented complete source writer, not historically attested or native validated. Pair consecutive exact source words. A canonical longest-common-subsequence alignment writes each matched letter once for BOTH words, and every unmatched letter with a LEFT or RIGHT role. A frozen78-entry prefix table over22abstract drawings encodes these columns inside one visible group. The reader rebuilds both words in parallel. This changes source word boundaries without storing a whole-word bank, fitting native meanings, or changing an old failed carrier.

design.mechanism: A reversible two-word alignment with explicit shared and unilateral letter columns. Matching is canonical and mandatory, rather than an optional abbreviation choice or a reference to a previously decoded word.
design.unit: Exactly one visible output group per consecutive source-word pair; a final odd source word uses an empty right partner only in the last group of its paragraph.
design.contrast: Not927preceding-word prefix copying,972common-suffix blocks,941vertical columns,1303fixed letter-pair permutations,1320optional fusion, or a whole-source-word dictionary. The source pair is decoded jointly; a shared letter can occur at any two ordered positions; every left/right assignment is written.
design.prediction: The complete output group has one unique prefix-code parse and reconstructs one ordered pair. Its number of column tokens is exactly |u|+|v|-LCS(u,v). Repeated complete groups within a paragraph encode repeated ordered source pairs, while similar source pairs can share literal column subsequences. No universal locality of edit effects is promised: the canonical alignment can change when a source word changes.
design.scope: Source-only exact spelling recovery over the explicit domain below. No Voynich symbol value, source-language identification, target score, statistical fit, historical attestation or physical manuscript binding is asserted.

source_domain.paragraph: An empty string or nonempty lowercase ASCII words [a-z]+ separated by exactly one ASCII SPACE. Source word order is preserved. No leading/trailing spaces occur inside a paragraph.
source_domain.message: A finite sequence of such paragraphs separated by LF. Consecutive and final LF preserve empty paragraphs exactly. The empty source string maps to the empty output string.
source_domain.excluded_input: Uppercase, digits, punctuation, accented letters, tabs and other characters are outside this frozen domain, not silently normalized. There is no unspecified escape branch. A new broader input domain would require a separately paid contract. Ordinary lowercase alphabetic instructions are meaningful source examples; the rule does not identify a historical language.

canonical_alignment.definition: For nonempty u and v, select a maximum-length order-preserving matching of equal source letters. Among all maximum matchings, choose the lexicographically smallest sequence (i1,j1,i2,j2,...) of one-based matched positions. This fully fixes repeated-letter ties; no output-shape optimization is allowed.
canonical_alignment.manual_procedure: Write the two words on scratch rows. A standard suffix matching grid L(i,j) records the maximum remaining number of equal-letter matches, with zero beyond either end. It can be filled using the two skip options and, when letters agree, 1+L(i+1,j+1). Starting at the two current positions with remaining optimum t, select the least pair (a,b) in lexicographic order with u[a]=v[b] and 1+L(a+1,b+1)=t. Emit the unmatched left prefix as LEFT columns, then the unmatched right prefix as RIGHT columns, then the matched letter as one BOTH column. Advance past the match and repeat. When t=0, emit the remaining left tail then right tail. For v empty, all columns are LEFT.
canonical_alignment.apparatus_cost: Two complete source words, up to(|u|+1)(|v|+1)small integer grid cells, and a78-entry letter-role table. This is hand-executable for short words but has a genuine comparison/memory cost; it is not claimed to be a historically used or fast shorthand. A greedy approximation is not part of the frozen rule.

physical_carrier.drawings: Twenty-two mutually distinct abstract signs d0,...,d21. The subscripts here are explanatory labels, not multiple visible characters or native assignments.
physical_carrier.column_alphabet: Exactly78values: BOTH(a)..BOTH(z), then LEFT(a)..LEFT(z), then RIGHT(a)..RIGHT(z), indexed t=0..77 in that order.
physical_carrier.code: For t<19 emit the single drawing d_t. For19<=t<=77 set j=t-19 and emit d_(19+floor(j/22)) followed by d_(j mod22). Thus19singleton entries plus59two-drawing entries are used. The remaining7possible two-drawing slots are invalid, not nulls or escapes.
physical_carrier.parse: A leading d0..d18 is one complete column. A leading d19,d20 or d21 consumes exactly one additional drawing. Any missing second drawing or unused table slot rejects the group. The three long-code heads can also occur as second drawings, so they are not exclusive group-initial controls.
physical_carrier.group_boundary: Concatenate all column codes for one source pair with no internal spaces; place exactly one ordinary visible gap between pair groups.
physical_carrier.paragraph_and_layout: Each source LF is an output LF and terminates the pair sequence. No arbitrary wrapping, hidden reset, continuation, or mid-group line break is permitted. A long paragraph therefore needs a sufficiently long physical line; no manuscript line-width fit is claimed. Empty source paragraphs are empty output lines.
physical_carrier.cost: Each alignment column costs one or two working drawings. No wordbook, numeral index, checksum, reference-state clock, extra marker sign, endword code or unwritten literal escape is used. The fixed78-entry table and scratch alignment work must both be taught.

writer: Reject source characters or spacing outside the stated domain.
At each source paragraph start, pair words1/2,3/4,... in their original order. If the word count is odd, only the final pair has v empty. No pairing optimization or source-dependent phase is allowed.
Apply the unique maximum-matching tie rule. Serialize the resulting LEFT/RIGHT/BOTH letter columns with the fixed prefix table.
Separate the resulting groups and paragraphs exactly as declared.
reader: Split the message at LF and each nonempty line at its single intergroup gaps. Reject noncanonical spacing.
Parse each complete group into the78letter-role columns. Start two empty strings u and v. LEFT(x) appends x only to u; RIGHT(x) only to v; BOTH(x) appends x to both.
Require u nonempty. Require v nonempty except that the final group of a paragraph may have v empty. If v is empty, every column must therefore be LEFT.
Recompute the frozen canonical alignment and column serialization of the recovered pair; reject if it differs from the supplied group. This rejects alternate alignments without guessing source words.
Return u then v when nonempty, join source words by one SPACE, and restore every LF. No dictionary, language model, native meaning or external expected plaintext is used.

source_only_hand_examples.reading: Append s,a,l,t to both words and the final s only to the right word; recover salt salts. Five columns, seven drawings.
The two different first letters are paid explicitly; old is written once for both words. Five columns, seven drawings.
An exact source-word doublet is legal and becomes one group; repeating this same pair later repeats the same group exactly.
The two LCS choices tie. Matching(u1,v2)precedes matching(u2,v1), fixing this alignment rather than choosing a convenient target form.
This is legal only for the final odd source word in its paragraph. The empty right word is recovered without a free marker or guessed word boundary.

source_free_proof_and_consequences: Each column preserves source order in both projections. Projecting LEFT/BOTH and RIGHT/BOTH therefore exactly reconstructs u and v. Prefix-freeness of the fixed code gives a unique column stream; the final odd-word rule gives a unique source token count. The canonical writer/readback composition is identity on the declared source domain.

Every equal-letter sharing alignment with b shared columns has |u|+|v|-b columns. Its matched positions form a common subsequence, so b<=LCS(u,v). Therefore even before carrier overhead any such writer needs at least |u|+|v|-LCS(u,v)>=max(|u|,|v|) columns. This writer attains that column lower bound, not necessarily a minimum working-drawing count among all alignments; it never optimizes the latter.

The total output length of a pair lies between the column count and twice that count. The frozen carrier's different letter costs can outweigh the saving from sharing. No compression ratio or length compatibility has been measured or claimed.

Every full group has a uniquely decoded ordered pair. Two identical groups imply identical ordered source pairs, including the special final odd case. Consequently repeated output groups do not implement a mandatory reference to the preceding group and are not automatically contradictory, but fixed-source pair-frequency and repeated-pair capacity are necessary obligations.

The source-word frequency multiset is not preserved because two words become one group; the multiset of the fixed ordered source pairs IS preserved by the injective deterministic group encoding. No claim is made that this escapes all1202-style capacity reasoning.

The relation between source similarities and shared output parts is inspectable, not universal: equal pairs yield BOTH-only columns, and matched source substrings yield identical BOTH code sequences. A changed source letter can alter the chosen alignment and many output positions. The design supplies a mechanism to evaluate, not an explanation of measured native residuals.
design.prospective_falsifier_and_scope: Before any native or source run, bind a concrete source, its paragraph segmentation and the unchanged grouping. The pairing gives exact source-pair repetition/frequency obligations and the LCS length lower bound without fitting glyph names. If those costs contradict a preregistered complete-message constraint, stop this fixed source/writer. For a separately declared fixed native sign key, every complete group must prefix-parse and equal the canonical re-encoding of its two projections; any failure is decisive for that key/contract. No such source, native key, corpus comparison, blind target or experimental gate has been selected here.
